description: Cluster Running a Kubernetes Version Past Standard Support
rationale: Once a Kubernetes version reaches the end of its standard support, EKS stops shipping patches for it for free: the cluster either sits in extended support, where fixes keep coming but at a higher price and only for a further limited period, or it is upgraded by AWS on its own schedule, which is an unplanned control plane change on a production cluster. The longer a cluster stays behind, the larger the upgrade becomes, since versions have to be crossed one minor at a time and each one may remove an API the workloads still call.
remediation: Plan the upgrade of the cluster and of its nodegroups to a version still under standard support, one minor version at a time, after checking the deprecated APIs each step removes
